title: Gold: more than Diwali shine
summary: Learn why families keep gold and why its price still moves.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Every Diwali, Nisha's grandmother adds a small gold coin to the family box. For many Indian families, **gold** is a way to keep value over many years, not just a gift or decoration.

The idea is **store of value**: gold has been wanted for a long time, so people trust it to hold worth when other things lose value, such as when prices rise across the economy.

But gold is not a sure-profit idea. Its **price moves up and down** with world events, demand and the rupee's value. For example, if 10 grams cost ₹60,000 and the price rose 10%, it would be ₹66,000; if it fell 10%, it would be ₹54,000. These numbers are **an assumption for this example, not a promise**.

Gold also gives no regular interest, and buying jewellery adds making charges. Gold can be one part of a mix, and like every choice, it carries risk.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: Why do many families keep gold?

options.text: It has long been seen as holding value

questions.explanation: Gold is trusted as a store of value over long periods, though its price can change.

questions.prompt: If gold costs ₹60,000 and falls 10%, what is the new price?
questions.explanation: 10% of ₹60,000 is ₹6,000, so the price becomes ₹54,000.

questions.prompt: Which statement about gold is correct?

options.text: Its price can rise or fall

questions.explanation: Gold prices move with demand and world events, so it carries risk.
